title: Imbalance-aware modelling identifies severe-crash patterns in Selangor records
summary: A study used Random Forest, XGBoost and SVM to analyze 6,978 fatal or serious crash reports from Selangor, Malaysia, covering 2012–2020,with one stratified 70:30 split and training-only class balancing. The selected class-weighted Random Forest had 81.66% accuracy but only 20.53% recall and 30.10% precision for serious crashes. Tree-model feature importance emphasized collision type, while other rankings varied by model; low-capacity motorcycle involvement was described separately through record frequencies. The dataset excludes minor-injury crashes and lacks exposure denominators, so these associations do not establish causality, population risk or transfer beyond one state and split.
ai_technology: Random Forest, XGBoost and SVM with undersampling, SMOTE or class weighting

evidence.tested: Dataset of 6,978 fatal/serious crashes (2012–2020), with 70:30 stratified train/test split and resampling/weights applied only to training data. The selected RF with class weights achieved 81.66% overall accuracy, serious-crash recall 20.53% and precision 30.10%. Feature importance ranks collision type highly for RF/XGBoost; road surface type tops SVM permutation importance. Low-capacity motorcycles are the largest vehicle share among the analyzed fatal/serious crash records, particularly loss-of-control on bitumen.
evidence.unknown: The analysis excludes slight-injury crashes, covers only Selangor, uses one train/test split, and has no vehicle-registration or vehicle-kilometre exposure denominators. The motorcycle frequency is descriptive and not evidence of increased per-vehicle risk; feature importance is not causal.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised classifiers with class-balancing methods improve recognition of the underrepresented serious-crash class and support model-based feature/risk-profile analysis of the 2012–2020 crash dataset.

source_review.scope: Original publisher reference PDF: cohort/severity definitions, stratified split and training-only balancing, class-specific performance, feature analysis and exposure/single-split limitations.
